scenes.title: Cold open
narration: The Heartbeat of Victory
This is Seungjeonmu. 1st century BC – present.
on_screen: Title card: Seungjeonmu · South Korea · 1st century BC – present

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The dance originated between the 1st century BC and 7th century AD, with early depictions found in Goguryeo wall paintings.
It was later codified as a military ritual in Tongyeong, Gyeongsangnamdo, and gained prominence under Admiral Yi Sun-shin during the Imjin War.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Originally performed to wish for victory in war and to reward soldiers, it is now performed at memorial services honoring Admiral Yi Sun-shin in the spring and autumn.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance is performed in two parts: a drum dance and a sword dance.
The drum dance involves four primary dancers and up to twelve others, while the sword dance features four women using two swords and long sleeves (Hansam).
The movement is defined by a pattern of three-advances and three-retreats.
Watch for Three-advances/Three-retreats.
on_screen: Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Circular, centered around a large drum.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The music is provided by an orchestra playing pieces from the Yeongsan Hoisang repertoire, specifically Samhyeun Dodeuri and Taryeong.
The primary instrument is the large drum, which features a taeguk pattern.
Listen for the Large drum, Traditional orchestra.
The music is characterized by the resonant, heartbeat-like thrum of the large drum, accompanied by the melodic, antique tones of a traditional court orchestra.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Dancers wear flower hats for the drum dance and archery cloths for the sword dance.
The performance space is centered around a large drum, and the dancers utilize Hansam (long sleeves) to accentuate their movements.
on_screen: Reconstruction imagery allowed only from the costume notes, labelled 'reconstruction'

scenes.title: The people
narration: Admiral Yi Sun-shin is the central historical figure associated with the dance's military application.
The tradition is specifically handed down from Tongyeong, Gyeongsangnamdo.
The dance shares origins with the Mugo of the Royal Court, both dating back to the Goryeo dynasty under King Chungnyeol.

scenes.title: A respectful note
narration: The dance is a ritual intended to purify the space and pray to the gods of earth and heaven; it should be approached with the gravity of a memorial or military rite.
